_meta.notes: SHAPE: attachment-is-the-schedule on BOTH sides - the 4-page PDF is cover, Summary Page, and two typed filer sheets. There is NO county Schedule A or Schedule B grid page anywhere in the document, so the wave hypothesis in the chunk file ('itemization is a typed filer ATTACHMENT, not the county Schedule A grid') is CONFIRMED, and specifically it is the third structural class, not a stub-plus-attachment. OCCUPATION: the attachment prints NO column headers at all on p3; the layout is [date][name][redaction bar over the address block][col-X][col-Y][$ amount], where col-X holds employer-shaped values ('Self', 'ATS', 'Fabian Vancott') and col-Y holds profession-shaped values ('Engineer', 'Attorney'). Both are captured, joined as 'profession / employer' - the county field's own 'Occupation/Employer' order, the same order used for the McAdams filing in this chunk - into the single county-form field Occupation/Employer, and each row note says so; the header names are NOT asserted because this page prints none. COVER vs CHUNK FILE: the chunk file's candidate/office/date/period all match the form. The cover's 'Office' box reads 'County Mayor' and the separate 'Office Sought' box is BLANK, so office_sought is taken from the top-row Office box (the documented 2008-era two-box substitution). The amendment question has NEITHER 'Yes' nor 'No' ticked - is_amendment is left '' (blank), never guessed to 'No'. PRIVACY: the address block on p3 is covered by a single wide black bar spanning every row - donor_city/donor_state are blank with 'redacted at source' on every contribution row; nothing was inferred from a name. Candidate's own phone/email on the cover are redacted by the county and were not read. Report received stamp NOV 01 2016.
